lane: write-regime-sm (perf-write-regime-fast, WAVE-6 probe-only; the standing [BACKLOG] per-host baseline state machine)
hypothesis: The fleet's flush-sensitive measurements keep hitting an uncharacterized host write regime (imageheavy's 6-97ms fdatasync band, record 20260929-035000; createwall's 1ms->65ms->245ms fresh-class crossing with the 65-refusal confirm-then-fire watch, record 20260929-150000): a per-host state machine with fast/slow/lifted states switching on minutes-hours scales underlies the advisory's DEGRADED flags, and lanes cannot tell a host state transition from a fleet event from a product effect. Characterize the state set, latency bands, dwell times, switching scales, triggers, and state memory on the standard fleet class; deliver the state machine model + the VALIDATION RECIPE (which windows are valid for which measurement classes; detect-and-wait vs detect-and-abort; expected dwell so watches can be sized).
approach: 3 fresh same-class VMs (hillclimb-regimesm-a/b/c, 16c/32GB/40GB ubuntu:22.04, provisioned together) + a light 60s control probe on the orchestrator box (the calendar's LOCAL-BOX control). Instrument = probe_regime.py (the hoststat census instrument, v0.9-structural, + per-sample statvfs fill), flock-guarded single instance, 6h continuous (2026-09-29T16:07:30Z->22:08:40Z): DENSE 0.5s ISOLATED fresh4k+sync_all+rename (advisory class 1, 37,390-38,127 ops/VM) + 30s rich dual-class samples (advisory class 2 repeat-fsync + fresh4k/64k/256k+sync_all+rename, fresh4k+fdatasync+rename, nofsync-rename noop control, append+fsync, cached-read, O_DIRECT controls; pre/post host counters; 633-637 samples/VM). ARMS: a+c quiet ambient; b + load_emulator.py (the working-churn arm: 16MB trickle/30s + 128MB build-cycle/5min, ~4GB/h, standing fill 0.005->0.287, the bench working-VM shape) — the H4 working-condition arm (both trigger instances were working bench VMs). Pre-registered questions/analysis in the lane DESIGN.md; time-based decomposition: fleet phases (all-VMs degraded) vs b-local episodes (b degraded, a/c healthy) vs the per-host state machine (remaining windows, log-space k-means on 30s non-stall medians, centroids >=1.6x apart, >=4% occupancy, the census method).
parity_notes: Infra lane, record only: NO product code changed, no product build measured; frozen parity surfaces untouched by construction. All claims are about host/storage infrastructure.

key_findings: THE WRITE-REGIME STATE MACHINE IS THREE DISTINCT CLASSES, NOT ONE: (1) the PER-HOST STATE MACHINE {fast ~1.0, slow ~2.6-2.8} flips every ~7-8min (slow med 2min/max 19.5min), lifts ONLY the fresh-write-rename classes (fresh4k 0.89->2.6-2.8, fdatasync 0.9->2.0-2.4) with repeat-fsync STATE-INVARIANT (0.63-0.66) - the census replicated on fresh hosts; (2) the FLEET INCIDENT PHASE (the trap regime event): all-VM onset within +/-8s, 12.5min this window, ALL flush-path ops lifted INCLUDING repeat-fsync (7.9-9.1, 12-16x) and append, nofsync/cached/O_DIRECT flat, traps 19-39% st50 / 7-20% st100 to 1.8-2.25s, matched to 0.1s across independent VMs, the tenant's own flush streams co-trapped (the load emulator's 16MB fsyncs to 1.79s), the orch box untouched => the shared sandbox-storage backend; (3) the WORKING-VM DEEP BAND (the b arm): 25 host-local episodes (b degraded while a+c healthy), ~19% of b's wall time, two shapes (lift-era elevated medians 3.9-14.7ms; burst-era fast medians with ALL-ops-stall and tails to 391ms), the createwall '~65ms class' reproduced (fresh4k 62.5/fdatasync 45.1 in the 17:59 episode), repeat-fsync FLAT in every episode (state-like, NOT the trap class), ZERO episodes on both quiet arms in the same 6h. THE DISCRIMINATOR (v1.1 rule B) SEPARATES ALL THREE LIVE: repeat flat + fresh lifted = host state; repeat lifted = fleet regime event; repeat+fresh fast with isolated st50/st100 = ordinary trap incidence. The fleet-sync evidence is sharpest at the trap level: a/c twin traps at 16:27:24Z (260.1/259.1ms, 0.1s apart) and the phase-max pair at 17:48:18Z (1799.7/2254.7ms, 0.1s apart) on independent VMs; 232 matched a~c stall instants (5.1x chance).
recipe:
VALIDATION RECIPE v1.2 (supersedes the v1.1 addendum's state rules; v1.0's stall-rate/max/host-relative/phase-model/no-ceiling core UNCHANGED; both probe classes at EVERY boundary, never back-to-back):
(A) THREE-WAY CLASSIFICATION at every leg boundary (fresh4k p50 AND repeat-fsync p50 from the same probe): (i) fresh <=2x its state band AND repeat <=2x its 0.55-0.77 floor AND stall-rate(>15ms)<=2% AND max<=50ms => HEALTHY (label fast or slow by the state band); (ii) repeat-fsync >2x its floor => FLEET REGIME EVENT - NO timing legs (any class), re-probe ~5min, expected phase dwell 10min-2h (today 12.5min); (iii) fresh >4x the fast floor (or all-ops-stall windows) with repeat FLAT => HOST DEEP STATE (working-VM class; on quiet VMs rare - treat as suspect; on working VMs expected ~19% of wall time).
(B) WHICH WINDOWS VALID FOR WHICH CLASSES: CPU/read-bound legs (parse/fold/render; the nofsync/cached-read controls are flat in ALL classes) - proceed in any state, label. Fresh-durability timing legs - proceed-with-label in fast or slow (the 2.8x slow floor is tolerable or wait ~10min: slow episodes med 2min, max 19.5min); ABORT in fleet phases and deep states. Single-durability-write absolute walls - fast/slow windows with pairing survive (v1.0 rule 6); in fleet phases ABORT (20-40% op-loss asymmetry defeats pairing).
(C) DETECT-AND-WAIT vs DETECT-AND-ABORT (watch-sizing - the createwall 65-refusal lesson): slow state => wait ~10min OR proceed-with-label (v1.1 rule C confirmed by dwell: med 2min). Deep state on a working VM => wait ~5min (episodes med 2.5min, p90 ~8min) - if bursts recur (clustered), abort/relocate. Fleet phase => NEVER watch for an exact-HEALTHY lull mid-phase: the phase traps 20-40% of ops continuously for 10min-2h; lulls are inter-trap gaps, not healthy windows; ABORT the leg, re-probe at 5min cadence, resume only on TWO consecutive HEALTHY classifications. Deep-state windows on QUIET VMs => suspect (0 observed in 6h): re-probe, then relocate.
(D) TRAP INCIDENCE is DAY-VARIABLE (0.75/h today vs 8.4/h census): never assume; the state-window floors (st15 ~0.3%, st100 ~0.003%) are the calm-day reference, not a guarantee. Matched-instant pairing across VMs (two probe VMs) is the cheapest fleet-phase detector if a lane runs one.
(E) WORKING-VM POLICY: a VM under sustained GB/h churn should expect ~1 deep episode/12min wall time (25 in 5.7h today), elevated isolated traps even when fast (0.58% st50 vs 0.03-0.06% quiet), and ~10x the deep-band wall-time; flush-sensitive campaigns on working VMs need the boundary probes at EVERY leg (the phase model) and should prefer quiet VMs for single-durability-write walls.
